title: Bluetooth & devices
blurb: Pairing, headsets, AirPods, USB devices not recognised.

remedies.title: Bluetooth device won't pair
remedies.why: The device isn't in pairing mode, it's still connected to another phone or computer, or the old pairing got damaged.

steps.text: Put the device in pairing mode (often hold the power or Bluetooth button until the light flashes). See its manual.
Turn Bluetooth off on your phone and other computers nearby so they don't grab it.
Remove the device if it's already listed, then add it fresh: Settings › Bluetooth & devices › Add device.
Remove the device if it's already listed (ⓘ › Forget This Device), then pair again.
Charge the device; low battery stops pairing.
Restart the computer and try again.

remedies.title: Bluetooth is missing or won't turn on
remedies.why: Airplane mode, a disabled adapter, a stopped Bluetooth service, or a failed driver.

steps.text: Turn off airplane mode.
Device Manager › Bluetooth: if the adapter has a down arrow enable it; with a warning sign uninstall it and restart.
Services › Bluetooth Support Service › Start (set to Automatic).
Shut down fully (Shift + Shut down), wait 30 seconds, start again.
Restart the Mac; if Bluetooth still says "Not available", shut down for a minute and start again.

remedies.escalate: If the adapter isn't in Device Manager / System Information at all, it's a hardware fault.

remedies.title: Bluetooth headset sounds bad in calls, or mic doesn't work
remedies.why: When a Bluetooth headset uses its microphone it switches to a low-quality call mode. That's normal; some headsets and computers handle it better.

steps.text: Use the headset's own microphone only when you need it; pick the computer's built-in mic in the meeting app for better music-quality sound.
Choose the headset (not "Hands-Free") as speaker when only listening.
In Sound settings pick the headset for both Output and Input together.
For daily calls, a headset with its own USB dongle gives the best sound.

remedies.title: Bluetooth mouse, keyboard or headset keeps disconnecting
remedies.why: Low battery, distance or interference (Wi-Fi, USB 3 hubs), or power saving switching the adapter off.

steps.text: Charge or replace batteries.
Keep USB 3 hubs and drives away from the Bluetooth device and the computer's side.
Stop Windows turning the adapter off: Device Manager › Bluetooth › adapter › Properties › Power Management › untick "Allow the computer to turn off this device".
Remove and re-pair the device.

remedies.title: USB device not recognised
remedies.why: A bad cable or port, not enough power through a hub, a missing driver, or a drive with no readable format.

steps.text: Try another port directly on the computer (not a hub) and another cable.
Try the device on another computer to see if it's the device.
Device Manager › look for warnings under Universal Serial Bus controllers or Other devices; uninstall the warning device and replug.
A drive that's connected but not showing may need a drive letter: Disk Management.
Open Disk Utility to see if the drive is there but not mounted.
Check the drive in DeskMedic's Disks page.

remedies.title: AirPods won't connect or switch to the wrong device
remedies.why: AirPods follow your Apple ID between devices and switch automatically; on Windows they pair like any Bluetooth headset.

steps.text: Put both AirPods in the case, open the lid near the computer, and pick them in Bluetooth settings.
Stop automatic switching: Bluetooth › AirPods ⓘ › Connect to This Mac › When Last Connected to This Mac.
On Windows: open the case, hold the button on the back until the light flashes white, then Add device › Bluetooth.
Reset the AirPods: hold the case button 15 seconds until the light flashes amber, then white.
